verses.zh: 彼勒屈身，尼波弯腰；巴比伦的偶像驮在兽和牲畜上。他们所抬的如今成了重驮，使牲畜疲乏，
verses.en: Bel[NOTE:1] kneels down,Nebo[NOTE:2] bends low. Their images weigh down animals and beasts.[NOTE:3] Your heavy images are burdensome to tired animals.[NOTE:4]
notes: Bel was the name of a Babylonian god. The name was originally associated with Enlil, but later was applied to Marduk. See HALOT 132 s.v. בֵּל.
Nebo is a variation of the name of the Babylonian god Nabu.
Heb “their images belong to animals and beasts”; NIV “their idols are borne by beasts of burden”; NLT “are being hauled away.”
Heb “your loads are carried [as] a burden by a weary [animal].”
verses.commentary:
46:1 "Bel" Bel (BDB128, KB 132, Akkadian for "lord" is a similar title to the
Canaanite title Ba'al). This is a reference to the chief god of the Akkadian pantheon
(Enlil, who was called "lord"). As Babylon came to power the chief deity's name was
changed to Marduk (BDB 597, cf. Jer. 50:2).

▣ "Nebo" This was the son of Marduk (named only here in the OT) who
was the god of learning and writing (BDB 612). He was the chief deity of the city of Borsippa.
Bel and Nebo can be seen in many of the Babylonian names of the period.

- Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:1)

- Nebushazban (Jer. 39:13)

- Nebuzaradan (Jer. 39:9)

- Nabopolassar (first king of Neo-Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar's father)

- Nebuchadnezzar

- Nabonidus (Belshazzar's father, last king of Neo-Babylon)

- Belteshazzar (Dan. 1:7)

- Belshazzar (Dan. 5:1)

These were the two chief gods of the Babylonian pantheon.

▣ "bowed down. . .stoops over" There is a play on the concept "bow down"
(BDB 505, KB 499). It relates to 45:23, the deities of Babylon are bowing before YHWH the Creator.

▣ "you carry. . .load. . .the burden" There is a play on the word "carry" in Isa. 46:1-2
and 3-4. First of all the idols of Babylon must be carried on beasts of burden to try to escape the
Persians or in ritual marches through the streets of the large cities. God carries His children, both
metaphorically in the womb and later, throughout their lives (cf. Isa. 46:4). It is the inability of the
Babylon gods to hear, to act versus the care, provision, and grace acts of the God of Israel, with
which they are contrasted in Isa. 46:1-4.

verses.zh: 都一同弯腰屈身，不能保全重驮，自己倒被掳去。
verses.en: Together they bend low and kneel down;they are unable to rescue the images;[NOTE:1] they themselves[NOTE:2] head off into captivity.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[the] burden,” i.e., their images, the heavy burden carried by the animals.
Heb “Their soul/life has gone into captivity.
The downfall of Babylon is depicted here. The idols are carried off by the victorious enemy; the gods are likened to defeated captives who cower before the enemy and are taken into exile.
verses.commentary:
46:2 "They stooped over" This is a play between the animals that carried the heavy cast
idols (v. 6) bowing down just like the idol's makers.

▣ "They could not rescue the burden" The idols could not save themselves (i.e. taken
by conquerors), nor could those who worshiped them.

▣ "But have themselves gone into captivity" Here these Neo-Babylonian idols are personified
as going into captivity with their people.

verses.zh: 雅各家，以色列家一切余剩的要听我言：你们自从生下，就蒙我保抱，自从出胎，便蒙我怀搋。
verses.en: “Listen to me, O family of Jacob,[NOTE:1] all you who are left from the family of Israel,[NOTE:2] you who have been carried from birth,[NOTE:3] you who have been supported from the time you left the womb.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “house of Jacob”; TEV “descendants of Jacob.”
Heb “and all the remnant of the house of Israel.”
Heb “from the womb” (so NRSV); KJV “from the belly”; NAB “from your infancy.”
Heb “who have been lifted up from the womb.”
verses.commentary:
46:3 "Listen" This, like Isa. 46:12, is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033,
KB 1570). See note at Isa. 44:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the remnant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

▣ "have been carried from the womb" This primarily is a reference to God as parent
and Israel as child. However, it also refers to the formation of the nation of Israel beginning with
the Exodus (cf. Deut. 1:31; Isa. 63:9).

verses.zh: 直到你们年老，我仍这样；直到你们发白，我仍怀搋。我已造作，也必保抱；我必怀抱，也必拯救。
verses.en: Even when you are old, I will take care of you,[NOTE:1] even when you have gray hair, I will carry you.I made you and I will support you;I will carry you and rescue you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “until old age, I am he” (NRSV similar); NLT “I will be your God throughout your lifetime.”
Unlike the weary idol gods, whose images must be carried by animals, the Lord carries his weary people.
verses.commentary:
46:4 "Even to your old age" God not only created Israel but will sustain her (i.e. "carry"
or "bear" them, cf. Exod. 19:4; Deut. 1:31; 32:11).

▣ "I shall be the same" This (lit. I Am He, cf. NKJV) is the concept that God
does not change (cf. NJB, cf. Mal. 3:6 and James 1:7). Even though Israel has been unfaithful to
the covenant, God remains faithful. He is the God of covenant loyalty. He is the same yesterday,
today, and forever!

For a discussion of "covenant loyalty" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "And I will bear you and I will deliver you" This is a reference to the
nation of Israel, but it is individualized also to every believer (SINGULAR VERBS). Notice
the VERBS in Isa. 46:4.

- God had created Israel (Qal PERFECT, BDB 793, KB 889)

- God will continue to provide and protect

- bear you ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 687, KB 741 (twice)

- carry you ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 669, KB 724 (twice)

- deliver you ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 572, KB 589

verses.zh: 你们将谁与我相比，与我同等，可以与我比较，使我们相同呢？
verses.en: To whom can you compare and liken me?Tell me whom you think I resemble, so we can be compared!
verses.commentary:
46:5 "To whom would you liken Me" This is the theological emphasis that no one can be
compared with YHWH (cf. Isa. 43:11; 44:6,8; 45:6). This is a comparison between YHWH and the idols
of the nations (cf. Isa. 40:18-20; 44:9-20).

Notice the parallelism.

- to whom would you liken Me ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 197, KB 225)

- and make Me equal ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 1000, KB 1436)

- and compare Me ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 605, KB 647)

- that we should be alike ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 197, KB 225)

YHWH is unique! He is the ever-living, only-living, one true God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM).
Also note the surprising NT theological revelation of Trinity, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

verses.zh: 那从囊中抓金子，用天平平银子的人，雇银匠制造神像，他们又俯伏，又叩拜。
verses.en: Those who empty out gold from a purseand weigh out silver on the scale[NOTE:1] hire a metalsmith, who makes it into a god.They then bow down and worship it.
notes: Heb “the reed,” probably referring to the beam of a scales. See BDB 889 s.v. קָנֶה 4.c.
verses.commentary:
46:6-7 These two verses are the contrast between the one true God of Isa. 46:5 and the idols of the nations.

- people give money to make images and then bow down and worship them (Isa. 46:6)

- they then move them here and there but they cannot move themselves; the idols cannot deliver (Isa. 46:7)

verses.zh: 他们将神像抬起，扛在肩上，安置在定处，它就站立，不离本位；人呼求它，它不能答应，也不能救人脱离患难。
verses.en: They put it on their shoulder and carry it;they put it in its place and it just stands there;it does not[NOTE:1] move from its place.Even when someone cries out to it, it does not reply;it does not deliver him from his distress.
notes: Or perhaps, “cannot,” here and in the following two lines. The imperfect forms can indicate capability.

verses.zh: 你们当想念这事，自己作大丈夫。悖逆的人哪，要心里思想。
verses.en: Remember this, so you can be brave.[NOTE:1] Think about it, you rebels![NOTE:2]
notes: The meaning of the verb אָשַׁשׁ (ʾashash, which appears here in the Hitpolel stem) is uncertain. BDB 84 s.v. אשׁשׁ relates it to a root meaning “found, establish” in Arabic; HALOT 100 s.v. II אשׁשׁ gives the meaning “pluck up courage.” The imperative with vav (ו) may indicate purpose following the preceding imperative.
Heb “return [it], rebels, to heart”; NRSV “recall it to mind, you transgressors.”
verses.commentary:
46:8 "Remember" This verse and the first line of Isa. 46:9 contain a series of IMPERATIVES.

- remember, Isa. 46:8 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 269, KB 269)

- be assured, Isa. 46:8 ‒ Hithpoel IMPERATIVE (BDB 84, KB 100)

- recall, Isa. 46:8 ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 996, KB 1427)

- remember, Isa. 46:9 ‒ same as #1

Number 2 is a rare form found only here in the OT. The Aramaic Targums translate it as
"take courage," possibly from a related Arabic root (cf. Leupold, p. 145).

▣

NASB
"be assured"

NKJV
"show yourselves men"

NRSV

"stand firm"

This Hebrew term (BDB 84, KB 100 II) is found only here.

- BDB ‒ found, establish

▣ "you transgressors" This shows that some in Israel still had doubts about the way
God was performing His task of restoration (cf. Isa. 45:9-11, the book of Habakkuk). This same group
is referred to in Isa. 46:12 as "the stubborn minded" of the Jewish people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

verses.zh: 你们要追念上古的事。因为我是　神，并无别神；我是　神，再没有能比我的。
verses.en: Remember what I accomplished in antiquity.[NOTE:1] Truly I am God, I have no peer;[NOTE:2] I am God, and there is none like me,
notes: Heb “remember the former things, from antiquity”; KJV, ASV “the former things of old.”
Heb “and there is no other” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
46:9 "the former things long past" This could refer to

- YHWH's ancient covenant with Abraham (cf. Gen. 12; 15; 17; 22; Isa. 43:18; 65:17; Jer. 16:14; 23:7)

- YHWH's acts of birthing (i.e. the Exodus) them

- Israel's ancient promise to be loyal and abide by the covenant (cf. Exod. 19:8; 24:3,7; Deut. 5:27)

- YHWH's proof of His existence by predicting the future (cf. Isa. 46:10,11; 42:9; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE [its uniqueness and inspiration])

▣ "For I am God" This verse uses two titles for "God."

- El ‒ BDB 42, cf. Isa. 40:18-42:5; 43:10; 44:10,15,17; 45:14,15,20,21,22; 46:6

- Elohim ‒ BDB 43, cf. Isa. 40:1,3,8,9,27,28; 41:10,13,17; 43:3; 44:6; 45:3,5,14,15,18,21

This, like v. 5, is a continuing emphasis on monotheism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A., C.

verses.zh: 我从起初指明末后的事，从古时言明未成的事，说：我的筹算必立定；凡我所喜悦的，我必成就。
verses.en: who announces the end from the beginningand reveals beforehand[NOTE:1] what has not yet occurred;who says, ‘My plan will be realized,I will accomplish what I desire;’
notes: Or “from long ago”; KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV “from ancient times.”
verses.commentary:
46:10-11 Again, God is using the example of predictive prophecy (i.e. the summoning of Cyrus II) to
show that He is in control of history. The emphasis on His purposes, mentioned so often in Isa. 46:10-11, shows
that history is not random but has a divine purpose (i.e. teleological; cf. Isa. 14:24,26; 25:1). This assurance of
YHWH fulfilling His Divine Plan is also seen in Isa. 14:24; 25:1; 40:8; 55:11 (see Millard Erickson, Christian Theology,
2nd ed., pp. 371-390).

The phrase in 10a is theologically parallel to Isa. 41:4; 44:6; 48:12. YHWH is
the "present one" from the "very" beginning to the "very" end (i.e. the first and last)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 我召鸷鸟从东方来，召那成就我筹算的人从远方来。我已说出，也必成就；我已谋定，也必做成。
verses.en: who summons an eagle[NOTE:1] from the east,from a distant land, one who carries out my plan.Yes, I have decreed,[NOTE:2] yes, I will bring it to pass;I have formulated a plan,yes, I will carry it out.
notes: Or, more generally, “a bird of prey” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV; see 18:6).
Heb “spoken”; KJV “I have spoken it.”

verses.zh: 你们这些心中顽梗、远离公义的，当听我言。
verses.en: Listen to me, you stubborn people,[NOTE:1] you who distance yourselves from doing what is right.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “strong of heart [or, mind]”; KJV “stouthearted”; NAB “fainthearted”; NIV “stubborn-hearted.”
Heb “who are far from righteousness [or perhaps, “deliverance”].”
verses.commentary:
46:12-13 This is a very important passage and shows that God will have mercy even
on unbelieving Israel. This shows that the Israelite people did not deserve God's love and mercy.
Many of them were still stubborn and stiff-necked (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORN, cf. Isa. 48:4), but God brought salvation to them because of
Who He is and not because of who they are (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). This is the New Covenant model
(cf. Jer. 31:31-34).

46:12 "Who are far from" This description of God's covenant people is contrasted
with the nearness ("it is not far off," Isa. 46:13b) of YHWH's deliverance

- through Cyrus II (temporal)

- through the Messiah (eschatological)

verses.zh: 我使我的公义临近，必不远离。我的救恩必不迟延；我要为以色列―我的荣耀，在锡安施行救恩。
verses.en: I am bringing my deliverance near, it is not far away;I am bringing my salvation near,[NOTE:1] it does not wait.I will save Zion;[NOTE:2] I will adorn Israel with my splendor.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “my salvation.” The verb “I am bringing near” is understood by ellipsis (note the previous line).
Heb “I will place in Zion salvation”; NASB “I will grant salvation in Zion.”
Heb “to Israel my splendor”; KJV, ASV “for Israel my glory.”
verses.commentary:
46:13 The Hebrew term "deliverance" (BDB 842) is parallel to "salvation" (BDB 448).

Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- H. C. Leupold, in his commentary on Isaiah, p. 147, reminded me that

- in Isaiah 14 the kingdom of old Babylon is judged

- in Isaiah 46 the idols of Neo-Babylon are judged

- in Isaiah 47 the nation, personified as a queen, is judged

- "Babylon," in the Bible, is imagery for all human society organized and functioning apart
from God (as is Edom in Isaiah 34). It is mankind's attempt to meet his needs with his own
resources. Babylon is personified as the great whore in Revelation 18 (which, by the way, I
think refers to faithless Jerusalem. See my new 2024 exegetical, verse-by-verse commentary
of Revelation [i.e. Partial Preterist]).
